In the <s>Elādi</s> group, the first mentioned is [<s>Sūkṣmailā</s>]; the other one is now described:
<s>Sūkṣmailā</s> (small cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum) — the other variety is now stated.

<s>Sthūlailā</s> (thick cardamom), and <s>Tripuṭodbhavā</s> (born from a three-valved pod).
<s>Spṛkkā</s> (Trigonella corniculata) [is also called] <s>Devī</s> (the divine), <s>Latā</s> (the creeper), and <s>Satī</s> (the virtuous).

children.translated_text: the <s>Śyāmādi</s> group destroys abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>), irregular appetite, <s>Kapha</s>, heart disease, and urinary difficulty (<s>mūtrakṛcchra</s>).
<s>Dravantī</s> (the flowing/purging one, Jatropha glandulifera) [is also called] <s>Undurukarṇikā</s> (rat-eared).
Those substances which [are listed] in the groups (<s>gaṇa</s>s),
in the compendium and in the abridged compendium,
having been stated, the scattered [i.e., miscellaneous substances]
The other [variety], having a very large tuber, is
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s> (the luminous one, Celastrus paniculatus) [is also called] <s>Kaṅguṇikā</s>,
[this is] <s>Pītadāru</s> (yellow wood, Berberis aristata) and <s>Haridruma</s> (yellow tree).
<s>Sitā</s> (white) — [this is] <s>Dūrvā</s> (Cynodon dactylon, Bermuda grass), also called <s>Śādvala</s> (verdant).
<s>Nīlinī</s> (the blue one) and <s>Cāraṭī</s> should be known —
<s>Śrāvaṇī</s> (of the month Śrāvaṇa) is <s>Muṇḍitikā</s> (the shaven one),
<s>Rasona</s> and <s>Laśuna</s> (garlic, Allium sativum) should be known.
and <s>karaṇḍaphalaka</s> — these [are names for the same plant].
<s>Bhavya</s> (the fruit of the bhavya tree) [is also called] <s>bhaviṣya</s>, <s>āmla</s> (sour),
Born of the ocean is <s>sāmudra</s> (sea salt);
born of the sap of the <s>mālatī</s> [plant].
<s>mādhvīka</s> is [that which is] made with honey.
[That made] with jaggery is <s>gauḍa</s>; with sugar,
the food of birds and sages (<s>śakuntamunibhojana</s>).
Two groups of five roots each
and <s>kaṭutraya</s> (the three pungents) — thus it is said here.
To be known is <s>carmapathika</s> (hide-traveler, i.e. bat);
A chameleon (<s>kṛkalāsa</s>) [has varieties such as] <s>mayūrādi</s> (peacock-type etc.),
and should be known as <s>gandhamūṣikā</s> (fragrant mouse)
[are names for] the house-lizard (<s>gṛhagodhikā</s>), also called <s>gaurī</s>
A monitor lizard (<s>godhā</s>) has the form of a <s>gaudhera</s>,
A moth (<s>pataṃga</s>) should be known as <s>śalabha</s>,
The wild [variety] should be known as <s>gavaya</s> (gaur/wild ox),
a bull (<s>vṛṣa</s>) [is also called] <s>kakudmān</s> (humped one), <s>gopati</s> (lord of cows)
A cow that has calved once is called <s>gṛṣṭi</s>,
The essence of food (<s>annasāra</s>) is <s>rasa</s> (chyle/plasma), the blood-
source, which is the firm tissue (<s>dṛḍhadhātuka</s>)
Flesh (<s>pala</s>) [is also called] <s>māṃsa</s>, born from blood,
[it serves as] the binding and supporting [structure] of the body (<s>dehasaṃdhānadhāraṇa</s>)
The essence of bone is marrow (<s>majjā</s>),
the oily essence (<s>snehasāra</s>) born from bone (<s>asthisambhava</s>)
<s>retas</s>, <s>vīrya</s> — [these are names for] the last tissue (<s>antyadhātu</s>)
<s>Ojas</s> (vital essence) is the essence of all tissues (<s>dhātusāra</s>),
of lunar quality (<s>saumya</s>), [and] the kindler of the heart (<s>hṛdayadīpana</s>)
<s>Māyu</s> [is a name for] bile (<s>pitta</s>), [also called] <s>vahnikānta</s> (beloved of fire),
<s>Śani</s> (Saturn) [is also called] <s>paṅgu</s> (the lame), <s>sūryaputra</s> (son of the Sun),
that is <s>Rāhu</s>, [also called] <s>Svarbhānu</s> (dazzler of the sun),
<s>Śambhu</s> (beneficent) [is a name for] <s>Śiva</s>, [also called] <s>Īśa</s> (lord), <s>Paśupati</s> (lord of creatures),
while a ripe one is called <s>phala</s> (fruit)
Attended by the Moon (<s>śītāṃśu</s>), Nectar (<s>amṛta</s>), and <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
born from the milk-ocean (<s>kṣīrodhija</s>) and lotus-born (<s>abjayoni</s>),
<s>Āśvineya</s> — these two [are known by both names]
